findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced this morning." followed by a `<ul>` with only three `<li>` entries (Beta Launch Plan, Holiday Campaign Assets, Partner Integration Pilot)
findings.fix: Either add the missing fourth project to the list or change the copy to clarify it's showing "3 of 4" / "recent" projects only.
findings.violation: The stated project count (4) does not match the number of projects actually listed (3), with no label indicating the list is partial.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no form action and no linked confirmation state
findings.fix: Add a "Settings saved" confirmation section/state (or at minimum a visible success message) that Save navigates to or displays.
findings.violation: Clicking Save has no defined destination or feedback, unlike the Invite and Archive flows which both navigate to explicit confirmation sections (#invite-sent, #project-archived).

findings.fix: Give the button visible text (e.g. "Duplicate") and wire it to a result state, such as a new "project-duplicated" section or a confirmation dialog.
findings.violation: The button has no visible label text (only an aria-label) and no href or target section, so sighted users see an empty control that appears to do nothing.

findings.evidence: Project name input value is "Vendor Onboarding", but the "Your projects" list in #workspace-overview-recent contains only Beta Launch Plan, Holiday Campaign Assets, and Partner Integration Pilot
findings.fix: Include "Vendor Onboarding" in the workspace-overview list (or explain in copy why it's absent, e.g. it's not "recent").
findings.location: section#project-settings, input#project-settings-name-input value; compare to section#workspace-overview list
findings.violation: The project currently being edited/archived ("Vendor Onboarding") never appears in the workspace's project list, so its origin and relation to the "4 projects" count is unclear.

findings.evidence: A submit button `Save` inside the form, plus a separate `Continue` outside the form
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single action (e.g. rename the submit button "Send invite" and remove the separate Continue link, or make Continue the only actionable control).
findings.violation: Two competing controls (Save vs Continue) both appear to finalize the invite action, but their relationship is undefined - it's unclear whether Save must be clicked before Continue or whether Continue alone sends the invite.

findings.evidence: `<input id="invite-member-email-input" type="email">` has no `required` attribute, yet #invite-member-continue-link allows proceeding to #invite-sent regardless
findings.fix: Mark the email input as required and block navigation to #invite-sent until a valid address is present.
findings.violation: A user can reach the "Invite sent" confirmation without ever entering an email address, contradicting the confirmation page's claim that an invite was sent to "the address entered above."

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted."
findings.fix: Display the submitted email address directly on the invite-sent confirmation (e.g. "An invite was sent to jane@example.com").
findings.violation: The confirmation text refers to "the address entered above," but that address is on a different section (#invite-member) and is never actually displayed or echoed on this page.

findings.evidence: "will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team" and "has been moved to archived projects"
findings.fix: Add an "archived projects" section with a link to it (e.g. from #workspace-overview or #project-archived), or remove the implication that one exists.
findings.violation: Both sections imply the existence of a separate "archived projects" list/view, but no such section or link exists anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: `<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` with no destination or confirmation
findings.fix: Provide a saved-confirmation state or inline success message after clicking Save.
findings.violation: As with the project-settings Save button, this control has no visible effect or confirmation state after being clicked, inconsistent with other completed actions in the document that show explicit confirmation screens.

findings.fix: Standardize on one suffix (e.g. always "-message") for descriptive paragraph ids across sections.
findings.location: section#archive-confirm paragraph id vs section#import-status paragraph id
findings.violation: Two paragraphs serving the same structural role (the section's main descriptive text) use inconsistent id-naming suffixes ("copy" vs "message"), breaking the naming convention used elsewhere in the document.
